fields.statement: Verified at 401ac36c0 as claude-code-0b7369d7. Read the diff: run.go adds queuedCheckMode (the start's own mode, else rhiza.daemon.permissionMode for a queued start, none for --foreground) and passes it to both checkAgentSteps calls in runRunStart; queueRunStart still records r.PermissionMode, so the queued start holds no mode, and daemonQueuedStarts fills an empty mode with the daemon's own. go test -trimpath ./internal/api/ -run 'TestQueuedCheckMode|TestRunStart|TestDaemon': ok (TestQueuedCheckModeStandsInDaemonMode covers Queued->manual, Named->plan, Foreground->empty; TestRunStartAgentRefusalsBeforeWrite still passes). go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/run-start-queue$' -testwork: PASS. In its log, with rhiza.daemon.permissionMode=nonsense, run start --workflow plan is refused with 'claude-code: unknown permission mode "nonsense"' (exit 2) and nothing is queued (the next start on the same change set queues without 'already has a run queued'); with it set to manual, run start --workflow plan --autonomous queues, starts.json has 0 permission_mode keys, and rhiza daemon --max-runs 3 --once starts it. I opened the kept work dir: the daemon-started run's journal for that change set records permission_mode manual and autonomous true, so the daemon passed its own setting. Minor: the script does not assert that journal mode itself; I checked it by hand.
